summary:
This tutorial covers `typedef` and `union` in C programming using Ubuntu 11.10 with GCC version 4.6.1. `typedef` allows users to assign a new name to an existing data type or user-defined type, making the code more readable and easier to modify. The syntax for `typedef` is `typedef existing_name alias_name`. An example provided uses `typedef unsigned int uint` to simplify variable declarations in a palindrome checking program. The program checks if a given three-digit number is a palindrome and outputs the result.

The tutorial then introduces `union`, which groups different data types into a single entity but allocates the same storage space for all its members. Only one member can be accessed at a time. A `union` example demonstrates calculating the total marks of a student with three subjects: English, Maths, and Science. The program calculates and displays the total marks, resulting in a total of 228. The tutorial concludes by highlighting the difference between `union` and `struct`: while `struct` can hold multiple members with different data types in separate spaces, `union` shares the same space among its members.
